page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, which translates to a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor to deliver dedicated CPU allocation.

This instance includes 300 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, offering high-speed local disk access directly attached to the host. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The processor supports hardware-accelerated instructions such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 support.

Benchmark results show average performance across several workloads, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1335.0 and a multi-core score of 5016.0. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is measured at 400.52 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write speeds drop to 33.9 GB/sec and 21.4 GB/sec respectively, which are categorized as weak. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests also show lower-tier performance relative to the broader market. However, the instance maintains average throughput for static web serving at 7.85 GB/sec and small-model LLM inference at 158.47 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5ad.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio coupled with high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring temporary high-speed scratch space without the overhead of network-attached storage. It is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, lightweight database operations, and basic text or image processing tasks.
